Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh and frame cap gives a noticeably smoother feel than 30 fps while keeping TDP moderate; bumping Texture Quality to Medium adds detail without a significant GPU cost. Expect occasional dips to the mid-30s in the densest hordes.

profiles.Summary: Warhammer 40,000: Darktide is a demanding co-op shooter that pushes well beyond the Steam Deck's GPU capabilities at native settings, requiring significant quality reductions and FSR upscaling to achieve playable frame rates. With low settings and careful tuning it can reach a stable 30–40 fps, though busy combat encounters with many enemies will cause dips.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 970/RX 570, well above the Deck's ~GTX 1050 Ti class GPU) and general Deck performance characteristics — check the frame counter in a live mission (not the lobby) and drop to Max Battery settings if the frame rate is unstable below 30 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling and a hard 30 fps cap keeps the APU well within 8 W, maximising session length. Half-rate shading helps further at the cost of some visual clarity during fast movement.

KnownIssues: The game requires an always-online connection for co-op play, which may drain battery faster and cause disconnects in poor network conditions.
Shader compilation stutters are common on first launch and may persist until the shader cache is fully built.
The game's minimum spec GPU (GTX 970/RX 570) is notably above the Deck's GPU class, so performance at any setting above Low is marginal.
Partial Controller Support is listed, meaning some UI elements or menus may be awkward to navigate with the Deck's controls.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Unlocking the TDP and GPU clock lets the APU boost freely, allowing Medium presets at 1152x720 with FSR to be mostly maintainable at 40 fps in calmer areas, but heavy combat will still push the frame rate down — do not raise settings further as 60 fps is not realistic on this hardware.

Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh + 40 fps cap on the OLED panel gives the smoothest motion the Deck can sustain in Darktide; FSR from 1024x640 keeps the image acceptable while Texture Quality at Medium preserves readable detail on enemies and environments. Reduce Shadow Quality to Off if horde encounters cause dips below 35 fps.

profiles.Summary: Warhammer 40,000: Darktide is a demanding co-op action shooter that pushes well beyond the Steam Deck's GPU class at recommended settings, but is playable at low/medium settings with FSR upscaling targeting 30–40 fps. The game holds a "Playable" Verified rating and ProtonDB gold tier, indicating it runs but may require tweaking and has some rough edges on Deck.
profiles.BasisNote: No dedicated Steam Deck or ProtonDB gameplay reports with settings detail were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 970 / RX 570 minimum, well above Deck GPU class), the Deck hardware profile, and the game's genre/engine characteristics. On your first run, check frame rate during a busy horde encounter and use that as your baseline — if the Optimal profile cannot hold 38 fps there, fall back to Max Battery settings.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 and rely on FSR upscaling to recover image quality; the 8 W TDP and fixed GPU clock keep thermals and fan noise low for longer sessions. Drop Volumetric Fog first if frame rate still dips in heavy combat.

KnownIssues: UI text and menus can be very small at 1280x800, making navigation difficult without zooming
Online-only requirement means a stable internet connection is mandatory; no offline play
Shader compilation stutters may occur on first launch or after updates
Performance can drop significantly in dense hordes or large open areas, making a locked 30 fps the realistic ceiling

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full 1280x800 native render at 15 W TDP pushes the Deck to its limit; expect the fan to run at full speed and battery to drain quickly. The 45 Hz cap prevents the GPU from chasing unachievable frame rates, but dense horde events will still cause brief dips to 35–38 fps — this is the realistic ceiling for this hardware.
